question: Can a conformal label-transition audit flag a few label-flipping federated clients among strongly non-IID honest clients more reliably than a standard cosine-similarity update-outlier detector?
method: Softmax-regression FedAvg over 20 Dirichlet(0.3) label-skewed clients, 3 flipping labels y->(y+1) mod 10; baseline flags robust z<-2 on cosine(update, median update); improved flags clients whose fraction of labels outside a 90% split-conformal set (leave-one-client-out ensemble, calibrated on a 10% hold-out) exceeds 0.3. Averaged over 3 federation seeds.
metric_name: attacker-detection F1 (label-flipping clients), higher is better
baseline: Cosine-similarity update-outlier detector: robust z-score < -2 on cosine to median update
improved: Conformal label-transition audit: flag clients whose fraction of labels outside a 90% leave-one-client-out conformal set exceeds 0.3
notes: Hyperparameters were fixed a priori and not tuned, so no CV selection was performed. The test set is used only for the final FedAvg accuracy. The paper's exact method details were not available; the improved model is a reconstruction from its name and description. Only 3 seeds and 20 clients per seed, so detection F1 is coarse. The digits dataset is a small stand-in, not the paper's data. Bundled data, so no download retries are needed.
